How a goal was scored, from its tracking

Source: R/classify.R
classify_goal.Rd

Reads a goal's tracking frames the way BluelineMetrics' goal types are built (bluelinemetrics.com): who released it, from how far and how hard, and whether it came off the rush, on a breakaway or an odd-man rush, as a one-timer, across the slot, through traffic, from behind the net or off the forecheck. Who did what is by NHL player id.

Usage

classify_goal(frames, team = NULL, goalie_ids = NULL, shot_type = "")

Arguments

frames

Tracking frames from nhl_goal_tracking().

team

The scoring club's abbreviation. Worked out from the frames when NULL (the club attacking the net the puck ends in), which needs a goalie in that net: pass it for empty-net goals.

goalie_ids

NHL player ids of the goalies. When NULL, each club's goalie is the skater who spends the clip closest to its net.

shot_type

The play-by-play's shot type ("tip-in" and "deflected" are never one-timers).

Value

A one-row tibble, or NULL when the frames do not show the goal.

Details

A skater has the puck when he is the nearest one within 4 feet of it for two frames running. The frames are turned so the scoring team attacks the net at x = +89.

  • rush: the puck was on the far side of centre ice within 5 seconds of the release (since, seconds).

  • breakaway: a rush the shooter carried over the blue line with no defender but the goalie between him and the net from there to the shot.

  • oddman: a rush with two or three attackers level with the puck or ahead at the blue line and more of them than defenders back.

  • onetimer: shot within 0.3 s of a teammate's pass, from more than 12 ft (tips and deflections aside); otpass is the passer.

  • cross: the puck crossed the slot (from one side to the other, 12+ ft) in the 2 seconds before the release; xpass made the pass.

  • traffic: a skater other than the goalie in the triangle from the release to the posts; screens are teammates in the shooting lane.

  • behind: the pass in came from behind the goal line, within 30 ft; bnpass made it.

  • forecheck: the other side's last possession, 0.5+ s, was in this zone within 5 s of the release and the puck never left the zone; fcwin is the teammate who won it back.

  • speed: shot speed (mph), the puck's fastest move in the 0.3 s after the release. passes: passes since the team last won the puck.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "goal-2025020534-777.json.gz", package = "bluelineR")
frames <- read_goal_tracking(path, 2025020534, 777)
classify_goal(frames, team = "EDM", shot_type = "backhand")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 25
#>      game_id event_id team  goal_frame release_frame shooter distance shot_speed
#>        <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>      <int>         <int>   <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 2025020534      777 EDM           99            96 8478402      7.5       24.1
#> # ℹ 17 more variables: since_neutral <dbl>, passes <dbl>, rush <lgl>,
#> #   breakaway <lgl>, oddman <lgl>, onetimer <lgl>, cross <lgl>, traffic <lgl>,
#> #   behind <lgl>, forecheck <lgl>, kinds <chr>, carrier <dbl>, xpass <dbl>,
#> #   otpass <dbl>, bnpass <dbl>, fcwin <dbl>, screens <list>
